title: Normalized strict derived tensor-model and evaluation data
statement: For a small ringed site $(\mathcal C,R)$ and its strict module towers [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], use their ordinary total tensors and normalized ordinary comparison data [def-sf-strict-tensor-ordinary-model-data], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and flat-term K-flat resolving objects [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], [def-sf-localized-strict-tensor-comparison-data]. Fix base and tower tensor presentations retaining the homotopy, derived, and two-sided resolving comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated]. Define a normalized computation datum, without asserting existence. It contains one-sided families natural in both homotopy variables, equal on two resolving factors to the inverse of the specified two-sided comparison [lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization], ordinary tensor-model identifications with their normalized homotopy descent, and ordinary, homotopy and derived evaluation comparisons. Require preservation of resolving objects by evaluation, the ordinary local-pure-tensor normalization, the homotopy comparison induced by that ordinary map, and the derived two-sided representative square using the fixed comparisons and exact-evaluation localization factors [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Require the one-sided evaluated square for every resolving $P,\Delta P$ and every unrestricted algebra tower $S$, and homotopy-input and coefficient-tower naturality. Define $\mathcal R_S(M)=\Delta_D M\otimes^L S[0]$ using exact derived diagonal, and define $c_{P,S}$ as the composite of its localization factor tensored with $1$, the supplied one-sided comparison, and the localized ordinary model map. Coefficient maps use the actual maps of degree-zero towers and recorded strict reductions. No flatness or K-flatness of the coefficient tower or surjectivity of its transitions is required.
